crucialFeats: One-inch punch demonstration at Long Beach.
Two-finger push-ups and extreme body control.
Creation of Jeet Kune Do through practical style synthesis.

dossier.advantage: Entry speed and cross-style adaptation. Bruce can break rhythm and strike from unusual angles before the opponent settles the range.
dossier.mentality: An analytical perfectionist. Bruce gathers information quickly, changes tempo, and looks for the shortest path to taking initiative.
dossier.style: A practical Jeet Kune Do synthesis. Bruce combines boxing, Wing Chun elements, and angle work into a system built to intercept movement rather than trade for long.

fighterA.name: Bruce Lee

powers: Elite human speed, reflexes, coordination, and precision striking.
tools: JKD interception timing, low kicks, rhythm disruption, and cross-style adaptation.
Short-range burst power, angled entries, and fast transitions between boxing and non-boxing attacks.
weaknesses: Significant size and reach deficit versus heavyweight specialists.
Lack of strongly documented experience against professional heavyweight boxing pressure.

crucialFeats: Wins his first world title at age 22.
Defeated 21 champions or heavyweight title challengers.

dossier.advantage: Heavyweight durability and ring control. Ali can make every entry cost the opponent more than it gives back.
dossier.mentality: A charismatic tempo-controller. Ali talks, provokes, and drags the opponent into a rhythm of his own making, then wins through patience and certainty.
dossier.quote: Float like a butterfly, sting like a bee.
dossier.style: Masterful control of distance and rhythm. His jab, feet, and head movement continuously reset the fight on his terms.

fighterB.name: Muhammad Ali

powers: Elite heavyweight boxing speed, timing, durability, and ring IQ.
tools: Jab control, footwork, defensive movement, clinch management, and pacing control.
Proven ability to survive punishing rounds and turn attrition into a weapon of his own.
weaknesses: Primarily boxing-centric toolkit compared with broader open-rules scenarios.
Vulnerability to low kicks and joint attacks that boxing does not account for.

battle-dynamics.label: Heavyweight Reality
battle-dynamics.phase_1: Bruce tries to enter on an angle and break rhythm, but Ali's first jab already shows the difference in reach, mass, and power.
battle-dynamics.phase_2: Once Ali has the timing, every Bruce entry becomes a gamble against a figher with huge advantage.
battle-dynamics.phase_3: The first truly clean Ali contact either ends the fight or decides it beyond recovery. Bruce does not have the physical margin to come back.
battle-dynamics.analysis: This fight does not honestly narrow into any real Bruce win path. Open rules do not remove Ali's heavyweight frame, range, or the force of his bare fist.

fight-simulation.label: Heavyweight Reality
fight-simulation.opening: Bruce tries to get in first and spoil the fight before Ali can set the jab.
fight-simulation.mid_fight: Ali does not need to chase. He only has to read the entry and land harder than Bruce can return.
fight-simulation.late_fight: Bruce has nothing that lets him survive the first truly clean heavyweight shots.
fight-simulation.end_condition: Ali ends the fight with a quick knockout or a brutal stoppage.
fight-simulation.phase_1_event: Bruce is faster, but not fast enough to disappear from Ali's jab line.
fight-simulation.phase_2_event: Ali reads the entry and lands harder than Bruce can safely absorb.
fight-simulation.phase_2_branch_a: Chaos does not erase the weight-class gap.
fight-simulation.phase_2_branch_b: Bruce has no physical answer to that contact.
fight-simulation.phase_3_event: After the first truly heavy shot, Bruce is no longer fighting on equal terms.
fight-simulation.phase_3_branch_b: This fight ends on his terms every time.

final-summary.line_1: Bruce is faster and more creative, but that is not enough against a heavyweight world champion with this much reach, mass, and durability.
final-summary.line_2: Open rules do not solve Bruce's problem. Every entry still carries him into Ali's bare fists, clinch, and brutal physical superiority.
final-summary.line_3: Bruce has no real path to building a fight where his own strengths have time to overturn the result.

tactical-board.lane: Bruce has no safe entry. Every attempt to close distance carries him into a heavier, stronger, and longer Ali.
tactical-board.subtitle: World Champion versus Artist

direct-verdict.line_1: Ali's reach, mass, strength, durability, and ring experience create too large a gap for Bruce to overcome honestly.
direct-verdict.line_2: Even under open rules, Bruce still has to enter the range of a man whose bare-knuckle contact would be catastrophic for him.
direct-verdict.line_3: This fight does not narrow honestly into 8/10 or 9/10. Muhammad Ali wins every time.
